key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can learn interpretable corrections to a simple turbulence closure, improving Rayleigh-Taylor mixing predictions during the transition to turbulence.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to upgrade RANS-based turbulence models for unstable stratified flows where standard closures miss early-time mixing-layer growth.
method: Embed a $k$-$\varepsilon$-$b$ turbulence model inside a surrogate PINN.
Use data-driven learning to calibrate coefficients and identify missing corrective terms.
Re-express learned corrections in terms of flow variables to obtain an explicit analytical closure.
evidence_signal: The corrected model is evaluated against an extensive DNS database of Rayleigh-Taylor flows and shows improved mixing-layer growth prediction.
watch_item: The learned closure is tailored to a specific transitional regime, so transferability to other flow classes or fully developed turbulence may be limited.
paper_title: Learning Turbulence Closures with Physics-Informed Neural Networks for the Rayleigh-Taylor Transition to Turbulence
